question: Find the value of sqrt{ (388 + sqrt{(127 + sqrt{289})}) }
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve nested square roots step-by-step from the innermost root to the outside.

√289 = 17

√(127 + 17) = √144 = 12

√(388 + 12) = √400 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = √(388 + √(127 + √289))

**Calculation:**

⇒ First, evaluate the innermost square root: √289 = 17

⇒ Substitute this back into the expression:

⇒ Expression = √(388 + √(127 + 17))

⇒ Simplify the term inside the second square root: 127 + 17 = 144

⇒ Expression = √(388 + √144)

⇒ Evaluate the next square root: √144 = 12

⇒ Substitute this back into the expression:

⇒ Expression = √(388 + 12)

⇒ Expression = √400

⇒ Expression = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Order of Operations for Nested Roots

Always start solving nested square roots from the innermost root and work your way outwards step by step.

Squares of Numbers ending in 3 or 7

Any perfect square that ends in the digit 9 will always have a square root ending in either 3 or 7. For example, 13² = 169 and 17² = 289.

Memorising Perfect Squares

Memorising perfect squares up to 30 helps to significantly speed up simplification problems in competitive exams.
